closure.note: Statement of record: gate 5 grades the constants the driver PRINTS, not the ones it USES; and the zero branch is tested before the luna88k branch, so BUDGET=0 prints a green row while removing the only work ceiling. THE MAJORITY DESIGN IS REFUTED - shared locals cannot kill an argument-expression mutant, because a local proves what the caller INTENDED to pass, not what the callee RECEIVED. The catch-up CAP is the protection; the ceiling is domain normalisation. Also: the report belongs at the CLAMP SITE (device context, where fatal() is already idiom), not in the handler - and the SIGALRM hazard codex worried about does not exist there. NaN is caught by NEGATING the comparisons that must exist anyway, at zero marginal cost: A FREE GUARD AT A TRUST BOUNDARY NEEDS NO REACHABILITY PROOF. Committed against shipping the loop bound alone, because interval=0 would then burn the cap every signal for ever.

MEASURED EVERYTHING, AND OVERTURNED TWO PROPOSALS. Built the offline driver and proved timer.c CAN be driven in the diff_*.c idiom (one stub: gettimeofday). CENSUS: emulated_hz is an int, so INT_MAX bounds every legitimate request - the ceiling is DERIVED, not picked. POLICY TABLE: 'drop missed ticks' is NOT A POLICY BUT A DEFECT (it caps every timer at 65 Hz - a 100 Hz timer runs at rate 0.65 with no burst at all); the flagship's cap of 65536 BREAKS a legitimate 4e7 Hz timer (1.0000 -> 0.1065); 2^20 is the smallest power of two that leaves every legitimate case BIT-IDENTICAL to shipped. Caught its own first probe (it held time fixed and would have cleared the defect).

SHIP-WITH-FIX. Sandbox denied execution, so MANUAL not CONFIRMED, and it said so.

REAL — one translate_v2p + one memcpy (memory_rw.c:87, :617-621); sharpening REFUTED: PPC lmw/stmw and lvx/stvx can already straddle

REAL - SETTLED. Measured: the :601 split is at 1 MB MEMBLOCK granularity (BITS_PER_MEMBLOCK 20), not the 4 KB page, so it fires on 1 boundary in 256 - a host-bounds guard, never a page guard. THE 'NO PRODUCER CAN STRADDLE' SHARPENING IS REFUTED at four sites: PPC lvx/stvx (16 bytes, NO masking at all), lmw/stmw, lwarx/stwcx, and the ARM arm_pop/bdt slow path (#357 made unaligned bases persist). None is LS_GENERIC_N, so #27's halt does not cover them.

OPTION A+C+D, and it BUILT THE INSTRUMENT rather than judging its feasibility. Compiled an offline differential of memory_rw.c on the first attempt and reproduced the defect immediately -- the key being that memory_rw.c has no PPC/ARM/SH flavour, so compiling with NO family macro excludes the MIPS/M88K/Alpha branches and leaves 4 headers, 3 globals and 6 stubs. Then MEASURED a four-variant table that settled the round: Option B is not a fix (a straddle beginning in a device still returns d0 d0 00 00); A alone SIGSEGVs on a 256 MB access because gcc does NOT turn the tail recursion into a loop at -O2 (~160 B/page); D is free and keeps the memblock split load-bearing. Also found TWO consequences the brief had missed: a straddling WRITE leaves the intended page unmodified and alters an unrelated one, and a faulting tail returned MEMORY_ACCESS_OK -- a missing fault. Verified the live trees untouched afterwards by md5.

OPTION A. Independently designed essentially the same probe and the same fixture, and gave the decisive test for A-vs-B before anyone ran it: a device handler that records (relative_addr, len). Caught that the Alpha offset_mask is 8 KB, so a naive 4096 split would be wrong -- the brief had said '4 KB page' throughout. Also applied R4's constblind finding unprompted: do not assert offset_mask against itself. Shell and git were blocked, so it read rather than ran and said so.
OPTION A composed with D, on the ground that B bypasses the split whenever the first page is a memory-mapped device -- the same failure the measuring seat then reproduced.

OPTION A, naming the device-dispatch failure concretely: a page-crossing access starting on a device-mapped page passes its full length to the handler, which returns before the memblock split is ever reached.

OPTION A with D, and LOOP NOT RECURSION -- it reached the loop conclusion from reading alone, which the measuring seat then confirmed with a stack-span measurement and a SIGSEGV threshold. Stated plainly that it could not read files or run anything.

OPTION B (+C+D) -- THE DISSENT, and it is recorded as such because it was settled by measurement rather than by the 5-to-1 majority. B generalises the existing memblock guard and is by far the smallest diff, which is a real argument; it fails only on the case where the access begins inside a device, which the measuring seat's D1 row then reproduced (d0 d0 00 00 against a correct d0 d0 bb bb). The flood surface ALREADY SHIPS (the handler fsyncs unconditionally today); the fix makes it at most ~3x, synchronous and single-threaded, so a guest cannot get asynchronous amplification. Not the cflood shape -- there the cost is a diagnostic, here the cost IS the semantics.

rows.title: hlen  Device handlers that ignore the access length (audit)
rows.hold: census done; promote to a FIX round?

closure.note: Opened from the b75 refutation, then characterized by census. A device handler that switches on the address and cannot service a width will read or write only the first register of an 8-byte access. MEASURED SCOPE: 62 spanning-capable handlers of 167 registered; 20 on machines this project boots. TWO BOOTED MACHINES ARE PROVABLY IMMUNE - SH-4 has no 8-byte access at all (fmov.d is two 4-byte accesses) and MIPS32/R3000A treats LD/SD as reserved, so landisk and pmax cannot produce the access. NO CONVENTION EXISTS in the tree: no helper, no macro, no rule - only three hand-rolled decompositions that are all big-endian-specific and that disagree with each other about the else branch, so there is no single idiom to copy. FIRST WITNESS NAMED: dev_irqc on testarm, the only spanning-capable device on that machine, where the two halves of one aligned 8-byte access have OPPOSITE legal directions (status is read-only, mask is write-only), which makes the miss unambiguous. DETECTOR SHAPE: an offline differential in the diff_*.c family - no boot, no rig, no serialization.

entries.note: CENSUS: 118 files, 62 spanning-capable handlers, 20 on booted machines. Coverage PROVED by set-difference against the 167 registered handlers, not asserted. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS NOT WHETHER len IS MENTIONED: 115 of 167 pass len only to memory_readmax64, which marshals bytes and does nothing about a span across two registers - so 'uses len' does not mean safe, and the naive definition undercounts the class about 15 times. Also measured: fatal() DOES NOT HALT (debugmsg.c:384 is a plain wrapper), so the 8 warn-then-service handlers are the defect with a log line.

rows.title: armbdt  ARM block transfer: the two paths disagree about an unaligned base
rows.hold: FILE - independent of the b47 fix

closure.note: The fast path masks the effective address while the slow path uses the raw address, so one instruction has two behaviours. Round #357 made unaligned bases persist, which makes this more reachable than before. Sites source-verified by the measure seat.

entries.note: *** TRUE, AND ITS 'ZERO SEAT ENTRIES' IS A LEDGER ARTIFACT, NOT AN UNASSESSED ITEM. *** OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md:2698+ ALREADY HOLDS THE FULL ANALYSIS -- verified independently by the main loop, which found the existing text naming the same mechanism. Re-verified the mechanism anyway: cpu_arm_instr.c:1550 fast path does p32[(addr & 0xfff) >> 2] (the >>2 truncates addr[1:0], which IS the architectural answer) while :1563 slow path hands raw addr to memory_rw -- same instruction, two answers, selected by PAGE RESIDENCY. Thumb PUSH/POP inherits it (cpu_arm.c:1670,1677). AND IT RE-CHECKED THE ARM CITATIONS AGAINST THE REAL LOCAL MANUAL, all three holding: LDM(1) p.A4-37, STM(1) p.A4-190, Table A2-10 'Operation unaffected by Addr[1:0]' p.A2-40 -- its own first grep reported them unverifiable and that was ITS error, caught by re-grepping. *** REPRODUCED, AND THE FIX IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. *** Probe built on the testarm/SA1110 cold debugger with a four-byte raw stub; every encoding re-verified through the emulator's own unassemble before any row was believed. Three binaries in a private tree:
* HEAD scores 9/15 rows against the architecture; MASK AT THE ACCESS scores 15/15; MASK AT ENTRY scores 14/15 and CORRUPTS THE BASE WRITEBACK (0x00070004 for 0x00070006). *** #357's 'mask at entry corrupts the writeback' is REAL, NOT FOLKLORE -- the mutant was built and measured. ***
* The divergence, three ways: the SAME LDM run twice against one page returns 0x77881122 then 0x11223344; ONE LDM WITH TWO REGISTERS returns r1 from a raw unaligned address and r3 from an aligned one -- MIXED WITHIN A SINGLE INSTRUCTION, because r1's own access warmed the page; and a cold STM SPILLS INTO THE NEXT WORD (0x00FF3344 / 0x5566FFFF).
* IT SIDESTEPPED THE `put w` WARMS / `put b` DOES NOT TRAP RATHER THAN TRUSTING IT: the slow path's own memory_rw inserts the page on its way out (memory_rw.c:732, no NO_EXCEPTIONS), so the first bdt access to a cold page is slow and every later one is fast. Running the IDENTICAL instruction twice makes the divergence a difference between two executions rather than a value that depends on trusting a seeding rule.
* FIX: two lines, cpu_arm_instr.c:1563 (load) and :1752 (store), addr -> addr & ~(uint32_t)3. Confirmed from the CODE (`uint32_t addr = *np` at :1514, `if (w_bit) *np = addr` at :1624 -- addr IS the writeback value), from the LOCAL manual (A5.4.2 p.A5-43; LDM(1) p.A4-37, STM(1) p.A4-190), and from the ENTRY mutant. NUANCE it caught: the Multi-word row of Table A2-10 is on the CONTINUATION page A2-41, not A2-40 where the table starts.
* IN-TREE PRECEDENT it did not expect: generate_arm_multi.c:117 already emits `addr &= 0xffc` and the generated combiners write back from the UNMASKED register -- upstream's own generated LDM combiners already use exactly this shape, and they fall back to instr(bdt_load) on a cold page, so they inherit both the defect and the fix. Thumb PUSH/POP (cpu_arm.c:1670,1677) call the same two functions; arm_pop/arm_push have exactly four callers, all enumerated.
* *** THE EXISTING GATE IS BLIND TO IT, MEASURED: arm_writeback_probe.py scores 22/22 on ALL THREE binaries including the ENTRY mutant that corrupts the writeback, and gate 14's 261 checks touch neither arm_pop nor arm_push. *** The single check separating the correct fix from the #357 trap is the W=1 writeback row. So the gate row is NOT redundant and must land in the SAME commit as the fix, being scored against architecture rather than against HEAD.
* Side effect named rather than left to be found: masking also removes the 4 KB page-straddle path for bdt, where a raw access at P+0xFFE currently translates once and takes its tail from the physical continuation.
* It also caught a records defect against the main loop: _scratchpad/CHECKPOINT.md had gone stale, naming HEAD 4d0981d and 'Tree CLEAN' when HEAD was 9bcae1c and two files were uncommitted. Re-derived.  [agent armbdt 2026-08-19]

RUNG MEASURES REACHABILITY-PROOF STRENGTH, NOT HARM. The carrier clause is corrected.

*** REPRODUCED AT RUNG 3 -- AND THREE OF THIS ROW'S CLAIMS ARE MEASURED FALSE. ***  The defect is real; the severity argument that put it top of a cluster is not.

THE WITNESS: unmodified in-tree `testppc` (-E testppc -C PPC750 -M 32), cold debugger, real guest instructions, real decode, real memory_rw. A PPC guest sets DBAT0 over a 128 KB window, sets MSR[DR]=1, and executes `stw r6,0(r5)` with r5 = 0x1201fffe -- unaligned, crossing the 1 KB split granule. Head (2 bytes) reaches the in-tree `fb` device; tail (2 bytes) has no BAT and no PTE, so a real DSI fires; a planted `rfi` at the DSI vector is the GUEST'S OWN restart. The same instruction re-executes, unbounded. Counters: one architectural store, FOUR device writes. **The trace is from a fully stock HEAD binary with zero instrumentation** -- the counters only counted. Controls all green: liveness (RAM through the same decode), DEVICE SIGNATURE (same program, only DBAT0L changed: PA->device reads back 0x3344, PA->no device reads back 0x0000), and a negative control two bytes lower that does not split.

CLAIM 1 -- 'not introduced by #430' -- MEASURED FALSE. Built from `git show 2458cfb^:src/cpus/memory_rw.c`, stock otherwise: the same guest program produces NO exception, NO restart, ONE device write. Pre-#430 the tail was silently mis-applied to the physically-following location -- the defect #430 fixed -- so there was nothing to restart. **#430 CREATED the fault, and the double-application is a direct consequence of it.**

CLAIM 2 -- 'the memblock split has had this property all along' -- MEASURED FALSE, twice. Post-#430 the memblock split can only fire on PHYSICAL accesses (a translated 4 KB write across 1 MB costs 4 translations / 4 host lookups; PHYSICAL costs 0 / 2), and its head can NEVER be a device in either version because device dispatch `goto do_return_ok`s first -- measured with a device straddling the memblock boundary.

CLAIM 3 -- '256x' -- MEASURED WRONG: it is **1024x**. The granule was measured by walking offsets, not read: MRW_SPLIT_MASK is 0x3ff, so 1 MB / 1024 = 1024. The 256 came from comparing 1 MB to a 4 KB page -- the granule this split does not use. *** THE SAME WRONG NUMBER WAS ALSO IN THE SOURCE, at memory_rw.c's own 'one boundary in 256' comment: ONE mis-derived constant became TWO records defects, and the row repeated it as a severity argument. Both corrected. ***

REACHABILITY IS FAR NARROWER THAN THE ROW IMPLIES, and this is why it re-ranks DOWN:
  * ONLY PowerPC can emit a straddling store at all. MIPS (AdES; swl/swr do an ALIGNED RMW), ARM, SH, M88K and Alpha all force alignment -- each checked in source. PPC's `if (addr & (LS_SIZE-1))` at cpu_ppc_instr_loadstore.c:229 is a FAST-PATH BAIL-OUT, not an exception, so the generic path passes the unaligned address through.
  * PPC is also the ONLY family whose device-failure path can restart: memory_rw's device-failure arm raises an exception only under #ifdef MEM_MIPS / #ifdef MEM_M88K.
  * THREE REAL GUEST BOOTS, instrumented: OpenBSD/pmax to root login, OpenBSD/luna88k to `login:`, NetBSD/macppc to the root-device prompt -- **ZERO straddling stores from guest code**. The seat first read macppc's 95 split-loop writes as guest activity and REFUTED ITSELF by logging the addresses: all are len=65536 at pc=0x0, i.e. file_elf.c:448's loader chunks running before any guest instruction.
  * Of the 1024 offsets in a granule only ELEVEN (0x3f9..0x3ff) can start a straddling 2/4/8-byte access, and the head's device offset is always within 7 bytes BELOW a 1 KB boundary -- so a register at offset 0x00/0x10/0x20 can never be a straddle head.

*** AND THE FIX MAY ITSELF BE WRONG. ***  Partial completion on a page-crossing misaligned store, with restart re-applying the first part, is what real PowerPC hardware does -- so gxemul may be CORRECT here and a fix may introduce a divergence. There is no PowerPC manual in _scratchpad/ (ARM, MIPS and m88k only), so the seat stated that as REASONING, NOT A CITATION -- the same trap CLAUDE.md records for SH. **Obtain a PPC manual before any edit.**

The minimal fix, if one is wanted: a dry-run pre-pass on WRITES only, walking the chunks with FLAG_NOEXCEPTIONS and committing only if all translate. Zero cost on the hot path -- it sits inside the `while (len > granule - offset)` body, which no aligned access enters. Watch TLB-miss handlers with side effects (PPC603 software reload) and do not let the dry run update referenced/changed bits.

Four more on the same rig, all CONFIRMED: dev_luna88k.c:816, and dev_m8820x.c:159 (read of CMMU_SCR), :152 (write to the read-only CMMU_IDR), :169 (write to the read-only CMMU_SSR), plus :125 transitively via m8820x_command(). Ruled out while checking: regs[] is sized M8820X_LENGTH/4 so the unconditional read at :145 is in bounds -- no OOB hiding behind the exit. The CMMU_CSSP1/2/3 example is REAL but weaker than first reported: m8820x.h says those 'only exist on 88204'. The 21-of-1024 gap stands regardless. memory_rw.c:572-578 already plumbs the #220 `cpu->running = 0` pattern, so the fix needs no new machinery.

REPRODUCED BEFORE ANY EDIT, and worse than filed. * Q4 -- BITS 25..0 ARE PROVABLY DEAD IN THE MODEL: luna88k_interrupt_assert sets bit (line+25) and devinit registers lines 1..6 ONLY, so interrupt_status can only hold bits 26..31 and reassert computes status & enable. No bit below 26 can affect any interrupt decision. So store-as-is and store-masked are behaviourally identical for delivery, and 'return without storing' is the ONE option that differs materially -- it leaves the old mask in force while the guest believes its SPL changed. Recommends store-as-is: masking would INVENT a hardware behaviour the tree has no source for. luna88k_board.h's INT_SET_LV0..LV7 are DEFINED AND NEVER READ -- the TIMER_EXTERNAL trap a second time -- though their nine architected values all have bits 25..0 zero. No LUNA-88K manual exists locally, so the HARDWARE meaning is an honest UNKNOWN.
* Q5 -- HEAT MEASURED, AND THE LATCH IS NOW MANDATORY BY MEASUREMENT: INT_ST_MASK0 takes **4,192,908 writes in 320 s** and 3,895,294 of them inside the 130 s boot => ~29,960/s during boot, 37% of every access to the device. The fatal() string is 76 bytes, so unlatched = **2.28 MB/s, ~296 MB per boot**, 6.2x the 4,849/s SCR rate already ruled cflood. And writes_with_LOW_BITS_SET = **0 of 4,192,911**: the exit sits on the COLDEST branch of the HOTTEST register -- the #433 shape exactly. Boot vacuity-checked (LUNA-88K BOOT x1, M88100 x1, login: x1).
* Q5 -- AND IT KILLED THE BRIEF'S OWN DETECTOR: 0x00000001 is the WRONG probe value, because the read path is odata = currentMask >> 8, so idata bits 7..0 SHIFT OUT ENTIRELY and the row cannot distinguish store-as-is from store-masked from not-storing. Use a bit in 25..8 and two writes with different architected prefixes. Plus four more vacuity paths, incl. a mutant that latches once then exits on the SECOND hit, which passes any single-store row.
* Q6 -- exitsweep must EXCLUDE dev_sh4.c:193 (the brief cited :191, which is the fatal(); the exit is :193). It is tick-only, reached from the SIGALRM handler via timer.c:283, so it is not even in exitsweep's class; timer.c:275-279 ALREADY records it. Landing the generic shape first makes it WORSE -- it keeps the unsafe fatal() and ADDS a plain-int latch written from both the handler and the main loop, a data race sigunsafe must then undo. The right idiom already exists: timer.c:65's volatile sig_atomic_t.  [panel_20260817_112300]

THE ADVERSARIAL FINDING, and it BOUNDS THE ROUND: the settled two-arm doctrine has a MISSING THIRD ARM, and a mechanical sweep would ship a worse defect than it removes.
* sh4_dmac_transfer (dev_sh4.c:340-428, DEVICE_ACCESS-reachable, exits at :372/:381/:390/:422/:427): the ONLY implemented CHCR_RS mode is 0x200, which by its own comment transfers nothing; there is no memory-to-memory path at all. Apply complain-and-continue and a guest programming ordinary dual-address DMA gets NO BYTES MOVED, CHCR_TE never set, no interrupt -- it polls TE forever or reads a destination that was never written. Silent corruption or a silent hang surfacing in a driver far from the DMAC, strictly HARDER to diagnose than today's exit(1), which names the mode in one line.
* AND THE LATCH MAKES IT WORSE, NOT BETTER: for a hot STATUS register latching is right, but for a STATEFUL OPERATION the first dropped transfer reports and every later one is invisible -- the latch actively SUPPRESSES the evidence of accumulating divergence. That inverts the #433 refinement instead of extending it.
* Same class at sh4_pcic's window-base registers (PCIMBR :917, PCIIOBR :926, PCILAR0/1 :891/:909, PCILSR0/1 :882/:900): dropping a write leaves the emulator decoding at the OLD base while the guest believes it moved, so every later PCI access lands at the wrong address -- possibly on a different device that answers.
* NOT A NEW CLASS -- #433's own adjudication hit it once (FLUSH_SUPER_LINE: a silently ignored TLB flush leaves the guest translating through a torn-down mapping) and solved it LOCALLY, without writing the rule down. So a mechanical pass over 170 sites would ship it at least three more times.
* THE ARM, stated so it applies per site: complain-and-continue is safe ONLY when the dropped write's only observable consequence is the register's own value. If the write's PURPOSE is to change how the emulator decodes, translates, transfers or invalidates -- address windows, TLB/cache flushes, DMA descriptors, coherency ops -- dropping it makes the model LIE rather than LAG, and the guest cannot tell. For that class: implement it, or stop honestly with cpu->running = 0 (which unlike exit(1) preserves the debugger and the emulator's own diagnostics) -- NEVER a latched drop. Three meanings, not two.
* AND THE ARM VINDICATES THE ROUND'S OWN SITE RATHER THAN BLOCKING IT: INT_ST_MASK IS state-changing (it is an SPL write), BUT the guarded portion -- bits 25..0 -- is MEASURED DEAD, so store-as-is drops nothing and the latched shape is correct at :816. That is exactly why this one site is safe and a blanket sweep is not.  [panel_20260817_112300]

rows.hold: Scope widened 2026-08-16 by the R6 pass-2 codex seat (read late): beyond the four listed defects it should cover external-event handling, reserved CONTROL-bit masking, and the retained/down-counter model. entries.note: UNBLOCKED: the 21285 datasheet was obtained (_scratchpad/dc21285.pdf, Intel 278115-001). Four defects are now specifiable. (1) SS7.3.41 bit 6: FREERUN wraps to FFFFFFh and keeps counting; PERIODIC reloads TimerNLoad; the clock source is bits 3:2 alone, identical in both. reload_timer_value() computes one rate and hands it to a repeating timer -- the PERIODIC cadence unconditionally -- so a FREERUN timer is too fast by up to 2^24/load. (2) TimerNValue is READ-ONLY (SS7.3.38/7.3.40) but the model accepts a guest write, and TIMER_1_CLEAR has NO writeflag test, so a guest READ of a write-only register reloads the counter and deasserts the IRQ. (3) Reset values diverge: hardware gives CONTROL 0x00 and LOAD 0, the model gives TIMER_MODE_PERIODIC and TIMER_MAX_VAL -- and this is the model bug #432's first draft mistakenly cited as evidence for its own zero mapping. (4) The random() counter model is now fully specified by SS7.3.40 + SS7.3.41 bit 7: a 24-bit down-counter, readable any time, RETAINED across disable and resuming on re-enable. The author's TODO is discharged; only a rig is missing.

Expand the item: external-event handling, reserved CONTROL-bit masking, and the retained/down-counter model belong in it alongside the four already listed. Ordering it after i8253zero would also be defensible, since i8253zero has a direct datasheet answer.

rows.title: i8253zero  A programmed count of 0 means 65536, not 'disabled' -- now datasheet-backed
rows.hold: settled by document; one-line fix in the hz computation

entries.note: SETTLED FROM A REAL DOCUMENT, which is the whole point of the item. i8253reg.h says nothing about a zero count (read in full, 102 lines), so the belief rested on memory -- exactly the trap this project names. The Intel 8254 datasheet (_scratchpad/i8254.pdf, 231164-005) states it twice on p.17: 'The largest possible initial count is 0; this is equivalent to 2^16 for binary counting and 10^4 for BCD counting.' So dev_8253.c:125's `else hz = 0` -- which the timer core then floor-clamps to 1e-8 Hz, i.e. never fires -- is wrong against the hardware convention. Cite it as the 8254, NOT the 8253: the count-0 convention was verified in the 8254 document only.

THE WITNESS: a cold-debugger probe on UNMODIFIED `-E cats`, the same mechanics as footbridge_sites_probe.py. Pre-fix and post-fix binaries from the same tree, same script:
  C1 liveness            0x11223344 both     RAM through the same decode
  A1 device signature    0xAA both           see below
  T1 negative control    halts at paddr=0x0c000043, MMU-on cannot reach it
  D0 count 0 -> hz       0 Hz  ->  18 Hz     the device's own report
  G0 guest-visible       IRR 0x0 -> 0x1      after a 1.9 s free-run
  D1 positive control    count 4608 -> 259 Hz, IRR=0x1, identical both ways
All four controls green in BOTH runs; only the two symptom rows move.

THE DEVICE SIGNATURE IS A VALUE RAM CANNOT PRODUCE, and it was designed against the exact trap that ate the footbridge probe's first draft. The guest writes 0xAA then 0x55 to the SAME address in 16-bit mode, writes the MODE register (a different address), then reads back and gets 0xAA -- the byte from two writes ago. RAM returns 0x55. Nonzero deliberately, because 0x0 is what an ABSENT device looks like.

TWO CAVEATS THE SEAT OWNED RATHER THAN HID: G0/G1 use a WALL-CLOCK window (1.9 s against a 55 ms correct period, ~34 chances), which is why the post-fix green is the settlement and not the window size; and its first T1 draft reported FAIL through a string-equality bug in its own script, which it found and fixed. All 27 instruction encodings were checked against the emulator's own disassembler before use -- the hand-assembled-encoding trap this project has hit four times.

REACHABILITY, MEASURED: no guest in this tree programs count 0. Every PIT write in _guest-src-openbsd22/sys/ is TIMER_DIV(x) (never 0) or 0xff/0xff, and no rig image boots an 8253 machine. A recollection that Linux's pit_shutdown() writes 0,0 was flagged RECALLED, UNVERIFIED rather than cited -- the right handling. *** BUT FINDING `pitflip` BELOW MANUFACTURES COUNT 0 FROM A GUEST THAT NEVER ASKS FOR IT, which changes the reachability picture entirely. ***

MAPPINGS, measured not read: cats and netwinder 0x7c000040; malta/maltabe 0x18000040; cobalt 0x10000040; iyonix 0x90000040; absent on prep, mvmeppc, algor, arc.

THE FIX is one line -- hz = (int)(I8253_TIMER_FREQ / 65536.0 + 0.5) -> 18 -- and d->hz[] is read only at :133/137/140, all inside the MSB arm, so the blast radius is that arm. *** DO NOT GENERALISE BY ANALOGY: dev_rtc.c:129 and dev_mc146818.c:409 look identical and are CORRECT -- for those devices zero genuinely means 'off', and dev_rtc.c's comment records a prior round reasoning that through. The 8254 is the opposite case. *** Minor: int hz[3] rounds 18.2065 to 18 (-1.1%) while timer_add takes a double.

rows.title: fbpending  footbridge pending_timer_interrupts is an uncapped int, never decremented by the tick
rows.hold: same class as #432, same registers; not a regression

entries.note: From R6 pass 2 (measuring seat, MANUAL). pending_timer_interrupts[] is a plain int, incremented from the SIGALRM handler with NO cap, and DEVICE_TICK never decrements it -- only TIMER_x_CLEAR (by one) and the disable path do. On cats (emulated_hz 50 MHz) a LEGAL load=1 with ENABLE accrues ~5e7/s and reaches signed-int overflow in ~43 s; four timers at the catch-up ceiling do it in ~7.9 s. NOT a regression -- the same was reachable before #432 -- but it is the same class as the bug just fixed, in the same registers, and #432's own text computes the 31 s figure while attributing it to a REJECTED design rather than to the shipped one.

rows.title: m8invread  The register-file arm invalidates EVERY translation on a plain READ
rows.hold: measurable today on the booting rig; may be hot

closure.note: Author self-review disclosed. Closed on: 21-row differential 0 failures, census 11 attempted / 11 killed / 0 survived / 0 faults with every kill naming its row, gate 2 PASS at 211 checks, site probe 9/9, and a luna88k boot 1:1:1 to login: with zero m8820x diagnostics on the FINAL built binary. Both pass-2 seats found surviving mutants and both were actioned.

entries.note: From R7. dev_m8820x.c's PFSR/PFAR/SAR/SCTR/SAPR/UAPR arm calls invalidate_translation_caches(c, 0, INVALIDATE_ALL) BEFORE the writeflag check, so plain READS purge every translation. PFSR is read on fault paths, so this may fire per-fault for a whole boot. THIS IS ALSO THE MECHANISM THAT CORRUPTED THE FIRST REPRODUCTION -- the offline driver left that callback NULL and six offsets crashed in the harness. Test-first: instrument a counter across a full luna88k boot on a scratch copy; if ~0, close as 'assessed, not changed'. If hot, move the invalidate under the writeflag check -- reads have no architectural invalidation semantics to preserve, and keeping it on writes preserves every existing correctness cue.

REPRODUCED TEST-FIRST, 4 rows / 0 failures, REPRO_M8INVREAD_CONFIRMED. dev_m8820x.c:304-314 groups PFSR, PFAR, SAR, SCTR, SAPR and UAPR and calls invalidate_translation_caches(c, 0, INVALIDATE_ALL) UNCONDITIONALLY, one line ABOVE the `if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE)` that stores -- so each of the six purges the emulator's entire dyntrans mapping on a plain READ. Measured 1 purge per register, 6 of 6, counted through an installed no-op callback rather than inferred. THREE CONTROLS HOLD, and they are what make it a measurement rather than a reading: the WRITE side still purges 6 (deliberately not under test), reading IDR from outside the group purges 0 (so the count is this arm and not something ambient), and the read still returns the seeded value 0xabcd (so a later fix cannot pass by turning the read into a no-op). WHY IT IS NOT MERELY UNTIDY: PFSR and PFAR are what a fault handler READS to find out what faulted and where, so the cost lands on the ordinary page-fault path, twice per fault. Per-boot read count NOT yet measured. THIS IS THE SAME CALLBACK whose NULLness corrupted the first m8820x reproduction by exactly six each way -- that accident was this defect seen from the other side.

*** TRUNCATED TWICE AS A SEAT FAILURE, THEN ANSWERED 10,431 BYTES IN THE FOREGROUND -- a HARNESS defect, not a quota wall. *** Backgrounding panel.sh kills the waiter and at least this seat; the verdict went to stdout only, so the run looked complete. panel.sh now writes $OUT/SEATS.txt plus a PANEL_COMPLETE sentinel. On the substance it ATTACKED ITS OWN PASS-1 ADVICE and got §6.2 right where deepseek got it wrong: the sibling PATC argument does not transfer, because m88k_invalidate_translation_caches walks vph_tlb_entry[] and does not evict PATC. It also named the brace-drop mutant that became row E7.
SHIP-WITH-FIX, and it COMPILED AND RAN rather than reading. Named the detector blind spot directly: double-read idempotency and PER-REGISTER checks, both of which became rows.

HOLD on §6.2 -- reasoned that the U/M writeback mechanism DOES transfer. Measurement says otherwise, so this seat was wrong on the conclusion; recorded as such rather than quietly dropped. It was RIGHT on the detector: an aggregate purge count misses a mutant that moves a purge between registers, which became E2/E4.

SHIP-WITH-FIX. Graded §6.2 honestly as UNKNOWN rather than guessing, and said which parts of its own reasoning were MANUAL vs BELIEVED. The honest UNKNOWN is what sent the question to measurement instead of to a vote.
SHIP-WITH-FIX and it named the right method: settle §6.2 by a before/after boot, not by argument. That is exactly how it was settled.

PASS 2. Found `if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE && idata)` -- ONE APPENDED TOKEN -- which SURVIVED all 16 rows: a zero write then neither purges nor stores, so writing 0 to a previously nonzero SAPR silently fails to disable that context. It survived because every write row used nonzero data and E8's single zero went to an already-zero register, so it was never a TRANSITION. Row E9. It also falsified a sentence I had written in the detector claiming a data-dependent guard could not hide, and listed seven records defects, of which the sharpest was that the comment asserted categorical non-visibility and then explained the mechanism of visibility. Disclosed unprompted that it is the same model family as a pass-1 seat (replication, not independent certification) and that its sandbox denied execution, so it graded runtime claims MANUAL.

PASS 2, AND THE HIGHEST-YIELD SEAT OF THE ROUND. It BUILT AND RAN three survivors of the 17-row detector. The sharpest restores the read purge under a value guard (`writeflag == MEM_READ && odata != 0`): it passed all 21^H17 rows, passed diff_m8820x.c, BOOTED THE RIG 1:1:1 -- and restores 144,536 of ~286,500 purges, HALF THE DEFECT. It survived because fresh() memsets the register file, so every read row reads zero and the guard never fires. Rows E10, G3/G4, G5 came from it. It also caught FOUR records defects, including two nobody else would have: three retracted sentences still alive verbatim in gate_offline.sh (the project's own grep-for-siblings rule failing on its first application), and that my "once per fault" CORRECTION was itself wrong -- it is twice, because memory_m88k.c:382-384 zeroes the non-faulting CMMU's PFSR so the handler must read both, which is why 49.98% of PFSR reads return nonzero. It ablated the compile flags one at a time and found -lm is NOT load-bearing while the unnamed -Wl,--gc-sections is. It classified one survivor (store-before-purge) as INERT rather than padding its count.

Implemented and closed. THE ROUND'S OWN LESSON: the detector went 4 -> 21 rows, and every expansion came from a seat BUILDING a mutant rather than reading the code. Two of the five survivors BOOT THE RIG CLEANLY, one of them restoring half the defect -- so a 1:1:1 boot is not evidence this removal is safe, and the file now says so. Eight records defects were corrected, all mine, including one where my own correction was wrong: a correction is a claim and needs the same evidence as the claim it replaces.

rows.title: m8online  Commit the cold-debugger probe: guest-instruction reachability, 3.1 s

closure.note: The detector the offline differential cannot be: it proves REACHABILITY, not just behaviour, and would go red under a change that unmapped the device. Structurally immune to the harness artifact that corrupted this round's first offline reproduction -- a harness fault emits no m8820x diagnostic at all.

entries.note: From R7. The committed differential proves the device's behaviour but NOT that the site is reachable by a guest instruction through the real memory path -- it calls dev_m8820x_access directly, so it cannot catch a change that makes the device unreachable (a memory_device_register length or DM_ flag change). The measuring seat built and measured the alternative: a cold-debugger probe, no boot, 3.1 s for 8 rows, ~60-75x cheaper than a rig drive, with every probe word disassembled before stepping. It is also structurally immune to the harness artifact that fooled the first reproduction: a harness fault produces no m8820x diagnostic at all. Rows must assert VALUES not survival (control r4 == 0x00a90000) and cover ALL FIVE sites, since a fix repairing only the default arm passes any detector that probes 0x800 alone. Do NOT add a booting-rig row: the fix is measured boot-neutral, so such a row could only re-assert what gate_ab already asserts, at ~200 s of load-sensitive wall clock.

SHIPPED. 9 of 9 rows survive a REAL GUEST INSTRUCTION through the real address decode and memory_rw plumbing, where five terminated the host before #433, each printing the complain-once diagnostic with its instance. VALUES NOT SURVIVAL: the first row loads CMMU_IDR and asserts 0x00a90000, the seeded 88200 rev-9 id, which can only have come back through the device. rows.title: ns16550  Guest-writable divisor divides by zero (UB) -- but not in the shipped build
rows.hold: REAL but optimisation-dependent; NOT the top item

entries.note: REPRODUCED TEST-FIRST, AND IT CORRECTS THE FILING AND MY OWN RANKING. Two seats filed this as the cheapest remaining guest-reachable HOST KILL on the live arc rig; I ranked it top of the queue on that. MEASURED: SIGFPE with a core dump at -O0 and -O1, SURVIVES at -O2, -O3 and -Os, and SURVIVES under the tree's own build flags (-fgnu89-inline -O3 -DNDEBUG). At -O2+ gcc exploits the UB and elides the division. So the host does NOT die in the configuration this project builds. Still a defect -- UB on a guest-reachable path, restored by any debug build or compiler change -- but not the cheapest host kill and not top of the queue. THE optrow CLASS ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THE GLASS: optrow was a DETECTOR following the compiler, this is a DEFECT following it, and any severity claim about UB must name the flags it was measured under. The vacuity check mattered twice over: read-back confirmed dlab==1 and divisor==0 at the division with debug() reached, so the negative is not a skipped path; and the first run had ALL THREE probes dying INCLUDING THE CONTROL, because calloc left d->addrmult zero and the access function divides relative_addr by it -- the harness producing SIGFPE for the wrong reason, separated from the defect only by the control row.

CONFIRMED from source independently: the divisor is guest-zeroable via the DLAB low-byte write and the divide sits in argument position of a real varargs debug(), so it executes at every verbosity. Its follow-on hypothesis -- that this shape has other instances -- is now REFUTED by measurement: 24 diagnostic-argument divisions in src/, 22 with constant divisors, and the only other non-constant one (diskimage.c:543) cannot reach zero. So ns16550 is the single live instance of the class, and a gate-6 ratchet keeps that true.

entries.note: The fold sends CMMU_FLUSH_{USER,SUPER}_SEGMENT to the all=1 arm. Safe direction, but NOT free of guest-visible effect, and the shipped comment claimed it was. A walk writes PG_U (and PG_M on a write) back into the page descriptor IN EMULATED MEMORY; a PATC hit sets those bits only in the PATC copy. So a guest that clears U on a page in segment B, flushes segment A, then touches B observes a U bit a correctly-scoped flush would have left clear. The tighter mapping needs no manual: match the walker's own 4 MB segment size, (sar ^ vaddr) & 0xffc00000. What real silicon does at segment granularity is UNKNOWN -- there is no 88200/88204 manual in this project.

entries.note: Per boot-to-login: PFSR 292,281 reads / SAR 612,186 writes / UAPR 13,026 writes; PFAR read ZERO times. (1) The read side is 99.999% PFSR, so the design brief's 'twice per fault' was WRONG -- it is once, and that sentence was inferred rather than measured. (2) The write side is 98% SAR, and m88k_translate_v2p never consults SAR -- it reads only SAPR/UAPR (memory_m88k.c:135,137), BATC and PATC. SAR is read at exactly one place, dev_m8820x.c:110, as the address operand of a flush command whose own arm already purges at :187. So a SAR write owes no purge BY EXACTLY #434's ARGUMENT FOR READS. (3) Registers that can really change a translation are 13,033 of 917,504 accesses = 1.4%; 98.6% of this arm's purges are unjustified and #434 removes 32% of them.

REPRODUCED TEST-FIRST and MEASURED ON MY OWN INSTRUMENTED BOOT rather than inheriting the assess-phase numbers. Per boot-to-login: PFSR 320,243 reads / 2 writes, PFAR 0/0, SAR 0 reads / 614,262 writes, SCTR 0/2, SAPR 0/5, UAPR 2/13,112. arm_purges 627,383 equals the sum of the six write counts EXACTLY -- the arithmetic control that the counter counts what it claims. Against the device's other purge sites (SCR 602,780, BATC 12) that is 49.9% of every INVALIDATE_ALL the device issues, so the filing's '98% of the write side' understated it.
CONFIRMED COMPLETE on the consumer table, searching every C and header file under src/ for all six constants. The only seat besides the measure seat to close the question rather than flag it as open.

*** CAUGHT THE DESIGN'S CENTRAL SENTENCE BEING FALSE. *** 'No consumer reads these' is wrong for SAR, which IS read at dev_m8820x.c:110 by m8820x_command(). Demanded three distinct reasons instead of one, which is what shipped. Also flagged that my FILING put SCTR in the translation-changing bucket -- also false, also corrected. And insisted on re-pinning E3/E4/F1/E9 in the same commit: 'a green diff_m8invread after this split is a stale pin, not a pass.' So the change is not a new assumption, it is an existing one applied consistently. It also gave the three-reasons framing verbatim and asked that the #434 comment block be carried forward adapted rather than deleted.

SHIP-WITH-FIX. Correctly identified that the brief's §2 grep only proves the NAMED-CONSTANT access path and does not rule out indexed walks, memcpy/aliasing, or access through cd.m88k.cmmu[] -- 'the single gap that could install a stale translation'. SHIP-WITH-FIX, converging with glm independently: the consumer table is right for direct constant-indexed access but four indirect shapes are unruled-out, and until those searches come back empty the fix is gating rather than cosmetic. Disclosed plainly that it executed nothing.

ITS OBJECTION WAS A REAL CONTRADICTION IN MY OWN BRIEF, not a misreading: packet §2 said PFSR is 'WRITTEN by the fault path; never read', while packet §3's measured table in the same document reported PFSR reads = 320,243. Both sentences were mine. The resolution is that PFSR is never read BY THE TRANSLATION PATH but is read 320,243 times BY THE GUEST through this handler -- two different senses of 'read' that the brief used the same word for. A packet-fed seat can only see what the packet says, and what the packet said was self-contradictory, so HOLD was the correct verdict on the evidence supplied. It graded honestly throughout: CONFIRMED for the arithmetic (it re-added the six write counts to 627,383 itself), UNKNOWN for consumer-table completeness (naming memcpy, pointer arithmetic, indexed access through cd.m88k.cmmu[] and aliasing -- the same four shapes glm and minimax named, which the measure seat then closed), BELIEVED for the SAR ordering while noting the packet never showed the SCR arm to confirm the purge is unconditional and per-CMMU. That last request was ALSO right: the packet had not shown it.

*** CLOSED THE QUESTION THREE SEATS FLAGGED, AND FOUND THAT THE CHANGE TURNS A GATED DETECTOR RED. *** Consumer table CONFIRMED COMPLETE by a CONSTANT CENSUS plus closure of every indirect shape: no memcpy/memmove/bcopy touches a cmmu struct; no escaping pointer into reg[]; reg[] is exactly M8820X_LENGTH/4 words with relative_addr bounded at registration so the index cannot reach batc[]/patc_*[]; the only code iterating the cmmu[] array touches batc[]/patc_*[] and never reg[]. It then read ALL of m88k_translate_v2p and enumerated its complete input set. HALF REFUTED: the filing says the spy 'counts CALLBACK calls'. It does not merely count. diff_m8invread.c:117-133 captures the RECEIVER, the ADDRESS and the FLAGS of every call, and derives inv_all_were_ALL / inv_all_addr_zero / inv_cpu_mismatch from them. Its own comment names exactly the hazard the row raises -- 'a detector that counts calls and ignores their arguments is green for any argument -- the constblind shape, and mutant A walks straight through it'. entries.ev: regress/gate_offline.sh selfmutant manifest; 11 diff_*.c, 5 covered, 6 exempt
entries.note: #436 covered five differentials and added a manifest so a TWELFTH cannot arrive uncovered -- negative-controlled: dropping a fake diff_faketwelfth.c in reddens the gate by name. The six on the exemption list are ieee_store (genuinely covered by gate 3, the only differential that ever had a failability control) and five that are REAL DEBT: sh4_tmu, wdc_identify, diskimage_io, diskimage_geom, diskimage_parse. Each is a detector whose every row could be inert with the battery green -- the exact defect #436 measured. The cheap half lands in one edit (the in-detector SELFCHECK row needs no mutant design); the self-mutants need one anchor and one named row each. NAMED rather than folded in, because two seats said explicitly that swallowing them in this round would break the stopping rule and leaving them unnamed would repeat the grep-for-siblings miss.

TWO OF FIVE DONE, and it found the PREREQUISITE nobody had noticed. *** diff_diskimage_parse.c HAD NO VERDICT TOKEN AT ALL -- it printed '37 rows, 0 failures' and nothing else, and selfmutant.py's first guard asserts the FAIL token is PRESENT, so NO MUTANT OF ANY KIND could ever be certified against it. *** Verified here: zero DISKIMAGE_PARSE_PASS/FAIL occurrences, and diff_diskimage_io.c has the identical hole. That is why the exemption list had six entries and no path to shrinking it.
* BOTH MUTANTS ARE DRAWN FROM THIS PROJECT'S OWN HISTORY rather than invented. diskimage_parse drops `&& !prefix_s` from #418's escape-hatch guard -- THE SEVENTH MUTANT OF #418 PASS 2, which a reading seat proposed, which was executed, and which SURVIVED ALL 35 ROWS; the row it now dies on was added to kill it. On every rig this project boots the term genuinely IS redundant (get_default_disk_type_for_machine returns SCSI for PMAX/ARC/SGI/LUNA88K/MVME88K), so it bites only on an IDE-default machine -- which is precisely what makes 'this term is redundant' a plausible good-faith edit. wdc_identify zeroes word 6's high byte, THE MUTANT #410 MEASURED SURVIVING AT ALL FIVE OPTIMISATION LEVELS, because #409 shipped the row with s=17 so that byte was permanently zero while the row's name claimed words 3 AND 6.
* Each reddens EXACTLY ONE ROW (1 of 37, 1 of 16) -- the diskimage_sync criterion.
* IT NEGATIVE-CONTROLLED THE APPARATUS ITSELF: a deliberately EQUIVALENT mutant (dropping `& 255` where the unsigned char type truncates identically) returned SELFMUTANT_FAIL, 'mutant applied but the detector did NOT report a failure'. So the two OKs are not rubber stamps.
* -std=gnu99 on the parse lane is the memory_rw hazard class, found by READING the compile lines rather than by being bitten: the gate builds that harness with -std=gnu99 while selfmutant.py's hardcoded CC uses -std=c99. Measured green both ways, so belt-and-braces -- but it makes the control compile what the battery compiles.
* GATED: offline-differential PASS 237 checks (was 235), seven self-mutants each killing via its named row, and 'no exemption is past its dated deadline' still green. SM_EXEMPT is down from six entries to FOUR with 11 days on the clock.
* Residuals it filed: diff_diskimage_io.c needs the same verdict-token fix before its own control is possible; and neither new harness carries an @@SELFCHECK@@ comparator sentinel, which gate_offline.sh:872 checks only for the original five.  [agent selfmutant6-B]

FABLE REGRESS ADJUDICATION of verdict_20260819_135703 at 6014b7e. Badge `s` disclosed: same-model adjudication of the main loop's records, not a two-family check.
* *** Q2 REFUTED MY OWN SUSPICION USING THE BATTERY'S OWN LOG. *** I wrote that no gate asserts the guest-visible CHECK CONDITION. Lines 554 and 559 say otherwise (verified here): `overlay: a failed sync reports CHECK CONDITION 2` and `nothing open: sync reports CHECK CONDITION, not GOOD 2` -- FAULT-INJECTED via fail_fsync_fd returning EIO, driven through the real diskimage_scsicommand() with a WRITE(10)-then-SYNCHRONIZE-CACHE CDB pair, not a direct call. So gate 2 EXERCISED the changed path discriminatingly rather than merely not breaking on it. The live gates ran the success leg for real: luna88k reached login in gates 5 and 7.
* Q1 MY FRAMING WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Too strong: the battery is NOT the evidence the harness commits did not break the emulator -- GIT IS. `git diff --name-only 1ba2cd4..6014b7e` minus regress/tools/docs leaves exactly the three #437 files, so no build input outside #437 changed and the harness commits COULD NOT have altered the binary. Too weak: the 16/16 IS evidence about those commits -- it is the first end-to-end execution of their product, 16/16 with 0 skipped means no gate silently dropped out, and the selfmutant controls DETECTED in this run.
* AND A FRAMING ERROR I REPEATED TWICE TODAY: diskimage_sync() does NOT sit on a path 'every rig's disk traffic crosses'. ONLY command 0x35 reaches it; ordinary READ/WRITE cross diskimage_scsicommand() but not the sync handler. The blast radius is narrower than I said.
* #437 touched THREE src/ files, not one: diskimage.c, diskimage_scsicmd.c, diskimage.h. 'One src/ COMMIT' was true; the round record should name the three files.
* Q3 NO EMERGENCY RE-RUN for 20ce22e and 7e3b120 -- every changed line is gate 2's surface or non-battery tooling, and the binary is bit-identical by construction, so a full battery would re-measure 14 unchanged gates against an unchanged binary: ritual, not evidence. ONE CHEAP CONDITION: selftest_mutation.sh's own header says run it after any change to gate 2, and that rule was triggered. Run gate 3 once at HEAD.
* Q4 VACUITY, NAMED NOT SURVEYED: (1) gate_asan_sweep is a CONSTRUCTION sweep -- 37 machine types construct under ASan and nothing more, so *** #437's NEW CODE HAS NEVER RUN UNDER ASan ***; (2) gate_hygiene's pattern set contains ZERO occurrences of sync/sense/sd0, so the new guest-visible error class is invisible to it; (3) gate_arm passed 16/16 WITH armbdt PRESENT -- not hypothetical, the measured LDM/STM defect was live at this HEAD; (4) selftest_mutation's green means ONE differential of eleven can fail, and its apparatus carries smhang/smnotland unfixed; (5) gate_ab is coarse rather than vacuous -- marker parity 1:1:1 accepted ~0.44% instruction drift. CHECKED CLEAN: gate_upstream's empty-both-sides hole is closed, gate 5 carries mutant-derived NINSTRS floors, and the old prompt-predicate hole in arm_flags_probe.py is CLOSED (its own 7-day-old memory note claiming otherwise is stale).
* Q5 QUEUE RISK THE BATTERY CANNOT SEE, ranked: armbdt (the only MEASURED defect, battery structurally green over it); idesync (the #437 CLASS on the other disk stack, and the ATA rig boots a ramdisk kernel that issues no flush traffic); b120r; the four wdc residuals including a guest-set malloc count behind CHECK_ALLOCATION; the three selfmutant apparatus items; and m437multi carries INVERTED risk -- the battery now PINS the conservative behaviour that item wants changed, so its fix round must expect a SCHEDULED RED, not a regression.

rows.title: reprowitness  The reproducibility rule asks 'can this MACHINE boot' when it should ask 'can this CODE PATH be executed'

entries.note: RAISED UNPROMPTED BY THE MEASURE SEAT WHEN ASKED WHETHER THE RULE IS TOO HARSH, and it is the most consequential thing on this brief. The standing rule -- no reproduction means DOCUMENT, not fix -- is right, but it is being applied at MACHINE granularity. armbdt is the proof: there is NO bootable ARM rig here, yet gate 14 already scores 261 checks on `testarm` through the cold debugger with a four-byte raw file. Machine-boot granularity would have DEMOTED THE BEST ITEM ON THE LIST. Proposed restatement: *reproducible = an executable witness exists*, with probe witnesses ranked equal to boots. IT LAUNDERS NOTHING -- dfreq still ranks last under it, because it has no witness of either kind. THIS DIRECTLY REOPENS THE exitsweep SCOPE QUESTION, which was settled on rig availability: sites in devices no rig boots may still have probe witnesses.  [panel_20260817_174701]

ADOPT-WITH-CHANGES. Probe witnesses on COMMITTED BINARIES equal boots; offline #include harnesses EXCLUDED. Supplied the governing principle the panel converged on -- a valid witness must preserve the HARDWARE SELECTION AND ROUTING MECHANISMS -- and a four-part anti-laundering clause: a witness is invalid unless it demonstrates a defect symptom on the PRE-FIX committed HEAD, records pre-fix failure and post-fix success with the same script, carries a positive liveness control AND an isolation control, and otherwise counts as documentation rather than reproduction. It also rejected the brief's own dfreq argument as insufficient -- correctly, though for a different reason than the one the measure seat then proved.  [panel_20260819_072053]

ADOPT-WITH-CHANGES. Right about the QUESTION -- executable witness, not bootable machine -- but the witness definition must exclude direct-call harnesses. exitsweep stays at one site this round.  [panel_20260819_072053]

PACKET. ADOPT-WITH-CHANGES: reopens exitsweep to probe-witnessed sites but bounds it by two qualifiers; 'an executable witness exists' is too loose as written and WILL launder.  [panel_20260819_072053]
PACKET. ADOPT-WITH-CHANGES, and the sharpest one-line formulation of the panel: 'executable witness' must mean an END-TO-END EMULATOR PATH, not a direct call.  [panel_20260819_072053]

PACKET. ADOPT-WITH-CHANGES: tighten to 'guest-reproducible witness' with an explicit anti-laundering clause; exitsweep may reopen but only against NAMED probe-witnessed sites.  [panel_20260819_072053]

*** OVERTURNED THE BRIEF, THE PANEL, AND THE SCOPE JUSTIFICATION OF ANOTHER ROW -- by building the witness the brief asserted could not exist. ***
* THE BRIEF'S ONLY ANTI-LAUNDERING EVIDENCE IS MEASURED FALSE. I wrote that dfreq ranks last because the footbridge has 'no witness of either kind -- no bootable rig instantiates an ISA bus or a footbridge, AND NO PROBE EXERCISES IT EITHER'. The first clause holds; the second is false and it built the counterexample in one session. `cats` constructs from the same four-byte stub gate_arm.sh uses for testarm, reaches the cold debugger, and `device list` reports a live footbridge AND a full ISA bus (8259, 8253, pckbc, ns16550, vga_ctrl, dec21143, mc146818). A real guest ldr/str then reaches it: TIMER_1_LOAD <- 0x12345678 reads back 0x345678, and THE VANISHING TOP BYTE IS THE HANDLER'S OWN SIGNATURE (dev_footbridge.c:548 stores idata & TIMER_MAX_VAL) -- RAM would have returned it unchanged. So dfreq does not rank last under the new rule; it moves UP.
* NEAR-MISS WORTH KEEPING: its first attempt returned 0x0 on every footbridge row WITH THE CONTROL STILL GREEN, because machine_cats.c:131 maps only the low 256 MB and the footbridge sits at PA 0x42000000 -- unreachable until the guest turns the MMU off itself. That run would have 'confirmed' the brief.
* AND IT WITNESSED A SECOND exitsweep SITE, killing the stated reason for that round's one-site scope: dev_footbridge.c:495-497, `case IRQ_ENABLE_SET:` on a READ does odata = irq_enable, fatal(), exit(1). Two arms of one script differing by ONE INSTRUCTION -- isolation arm survives with both controls green, kill arm exits 1 with the WARNING text. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY at those lines. The table row 'reproducible by BOOTING a rig we have -- ONE' is correct as written, but it is NOT the same claim as 'reproducible -- ONE', and it has been read as the second. Seven more footbridge sites sit in the same 0x400 window.
* *** THE PROPOSED ANTI-LAUNDERING CLAUSE REJECTS THE PROJECT'S OWN EXEMPLAR. *** regress/m8820x_sites_probe.py states the panel's governing principle VERBATIM and is where the principle comes from -- yet it shipped as 9494c6a, THREE COMMITS AFTER the #433 fix 66b0367 (verified), with every row SURVIVED, post-fix only. It satisfies neither clause (1) 'defect symptom on the pre-fix HEAD' nor clause (2) 'pre-fix failure and post-fix success'. The principle was lifted out of a DETECTOR and is being written as a rule for WITNESSES.
* SO THE DETECTOR/WITNESS DISTINCTION IS NOT NEW -- it is committed, in that file's own comment, together with its cost argument (3.2 s cold-debugger vs 182-233 s for a rig drive, ~60x cheaper). Where the project conflates them is not in its ENGINEERING but in its RECORDS: round prose says 'reproduced' without naming the artefact.
* A MISSING RUNG, and it names where laundering will actually happen: the real ladder is (1) #include harness -- behaviour only, rejected; (2) MACHINE CONSTRUCTION -- device registered in the address map, no guest instruction, WHICH THE RULE IS SILENT ABOUT and gate 9 already does for every machine type; (3) cold-debugger probe -- real instruction, real decode; (4) boot -- a real driver reaches it unaided.
* DROP 'EQUAL': a probe proves a path CAN be reached (right for a bounds fix); a boot proves it IS travelled (right for RANKING). #437 is the illustration -- its luna88k boot showed SYNCHRONIZE CACHE is issued once per boot right after MARKING FILE SYSTEM CLEAN, which no probe could produce. Admissible-equal, subordinate for prioritisation.
* RETROACTIVE COST: ZERO closed rows are invalidated (85 rows, 16 closed, scanned). But the check is weaker than it looks and THE REAL FINDING IS A SCHEMA GAP -- the ledger has no field naming WHICH ARTEFACT WITNESSED THE DEFECT, so the question is answerable only by reading prose. b47/#47 is the closest call: its defect witness is the #include differential ('15 of 23 red against the pre-change file') and its boots are no-regression checks, not defect witnesses.
* STUBBING DEMONSTRABLY DISTORTS: m8820x's offline reproduction reported 1013/1015/11 where the true numbers are 1007/1009/17 -- a stub artefact, because the harness left invalidate_translation_caches NULL and that callback fires on reads too. The one round that reproduced offline got its numbers wrong, in the direction the principle predicts.
* AGREES exitsweep stays at ONE SITE, but on a different and stronger ground: not 'only one is reproducible' (false) but the THIRD DOCTRINE ARM, which bounds it on SEMANTICS and does not evaporate when someone writes a probe. Proposed reopening rule: add a second site only when it is witnessed, in the SAME DEVICE and SAME SEMANTIC CLASS so one fix design covers both, and covered by the SAME DETECTOR without a new oracle -- under which the eight footbridge sites are ONE candidate round, not eight.  [panel_20260819_072053]

*** SUPPLIED THE DISCRIMINATOR THE OTHER SIX SEATS DID NOT: A TEST, NOT A DEFINITION. *** 'If your reproduction still compiles and still fails after the in-tree machine description and the CPU/device dispatch are removed -- leaving only a direct call -- IT WAS NEVER A REPRODUCTION.' That is mechanically checkable, where 'preserves routing' still needs judgement. Its one-sentence laundering test is the same idea sharpened: 'I can write a probe that calls this function' is not a reproduction, it is A RESTATEMENT OF THE SOURCE.
* It also enumerated what does NOT count: an #include harness calling a handler or helper; a machine or device_add introduced IN ORDER TO reach the site; a detector or self-mutant; a source reading. And it drew the timing line explicitly -- detectors of the #include/--wrap kind MAY ship AFTER a witness exists; they do not CREATE one. That is the cleanest statement of the detector/witness split anyone gave.
* Q5 SEQUENCING, and it is the operationally decisive part: exitsweep MAY implement dev_luna88k.c:816 under the CURRENT rule, because that site is legal on both readings -- blocking it on a debate about the complement 'starves the only measured kill'. * And on who decides: 'the panel should not pretend a vote is a measurement' -- the standing-text change is the flagship/owner's to record. That independently supports the owner's call on 2026-08-19 to wait for Fable's adjudication rather than adopt on 5-of-6.
* RECORDED LATE, and caught by precommit section G rather than by me: grok does not lead with a VERDICT line, so my grep-based triage dropped it -- the SECOND time, after the same miss on the #437 pass 2. The triage habit is the defect, not the seat.  [panel_20260819_072053]

rows.title: m437ord  The #437 ordering rule is reviewed but NOT gated -- it needs one fault-injection row

entries.note: Deleting the ordering `continue` in diskimage_sync() is the one mutant the shipped detector does not catch. The pass-2 measure seat VERIFIED a row can catch it: inject an fsync failure on the overlay data file and assert the bitmap fd is ABSENT from the trace -- shipped syncs fds [4 5 6], the mutant syncs [4 5 6 7]. One row, not built.  [panel_20260818_095322]

BUILT AND CLOSED, and it IMPROVED ON THE RECIPE IT WAS GIVEN. Told to build the single-overlay row a prior pass had specified, it built that, then probed two SIBLING mutants and measured that the single-overlay row catches ONLY the deletion: `continue` -> `break;` and `continue` -> `return 0;` both pass it GREEN, because with one overlay there is no next iteration and all three mutants trace identically. A SECOND OVERLAY separates them and one row kills all three. It supplied both patches and recommended the stronger, which also perturbs no existing gate check where the fallback would have forced one from "1" to "2".
* Mechanism: __wrap_fsync consults a static fail_fsync_fd, sets errno=EIO and returns -1 without calling __real_fsync; armed after the WRITE, disarmed when the command returns. It rejected, with reasons written into the file, a real failing fsync (needs dm-error/root, non-portable -- same class as the drvfs trap), close()ing the fd under the live FILE* (a FAULT, and can hit a recycled fd) and an O_RDONLY fd (rc 0 on glibc, proves nothing).
* A CRASH IS NOT WHAT MAKES IT FAIL, measured four ways: rc is 1 never >=128; the mutant printed all 11 rows plus the verdict line so it reached the end of main; ASan+UBSan produced 0 bytes on both arms; and exactly one row differs, by a printed string.
* INSTRUMENT-SABOTAGE CONTROL (`if (0 && fd == fail_fsync_fd)`) turns TWO rows red, so a dead injection fails loudly and the signatures are distinguishable: two red together = the instrument, the ordering row red alone = the code.
* VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE MAIN LOOP, and MY FIRST THREE ATTEMPTS WERE ALL VOID -- the loop variable was eaten before reaching WSL and the printed rc was grep's status; then the anchor took 'the first continue in a range' when the loop has TWO and the f_data==NULL branch never executes, so all three mutants 'passed' and would have discredited the row; then anchoring on the fsync call matched :1211 in overlay_set_block_in_use, a different function. Only a context printout of the line about to be mutated caught it. Correctly anchored on the unique 'Data is not durable' comment: ALL THREE MUTANTS KILLED, traces distinguishable -- deleted publishes b0 anyway, break/return0 stop at F(d0) S(d0).
* Gate 2: PASS 235 checks (was 231). Honest limits recorded in the file: the CHECK-CONDITION row is a WITNESS not a discriminator (green on every code mutant); an fflush failure on the data file is not injected, only fsync; and the injection skips the real fsync, so a partially-successful sync is UNTESTED and UNKNOWN.  [agent m437ord 2026-08-19]

FABLE REGRESS ADJUDICATION of verdict_20260819_135703 at 6014b7e. Badge `s` disclosed: same-model adjudication of the main loop's records, not a two-family check.
* *** Q2 REFUTED MY OWN SUSPICION USING THE BATTERY'S OWN LOG. *** I wrote that no gate asserts the guest-visible CHECK CONDITION. Lines 554 and 559 say otherwise (verified here): `overlay: a failed sync reports CHECK CONDITION 2` and `nothing open: sync reports CHECK CONDITION, not GOOD 2` -- FAULT-INJECTED via fail_fsync_fd returning EIO, driven through the real diskimage_scsicommand() with a WRITE(10)-then-SYNCHRONIZE-CACHE CDB pair, not a direct call. So gate 2 EXERCISED the changed path discriminatingly rather than merely not breaking on it. The live gates ran the success leg for real: luna88k reached login in gates 5 and 7.
* Q1 MY FRAMING WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Too strong: the battery is NOT the evidence the harness commits did not break the emulator -- GIT IS. `git diff --name-only 1ba2cd4..6014b7e` minus regress/tools/docs leaves exactly the three #437 files, so no build input outside #437 changed and the harness commits COULD NOT have altered the binary. Too weak: the 16/16 IS evidence about those commits -- it is the first end-to-end execution of their product, 16/16 with 0 skipped means no gate silently dropped out, and the selfmutant controls DETECTED in this run.
* AND A FRAMING ERROR I REPEATED TWICE TODAY: diskimage_sync() does NOT sit on a path 'every rig's disk traffic crosses'. ONLY command 0x35 reaches it; ordinary READ/WRITE cross diskimage_scsicommand() but not the sync handler. The blast radius is narrower than I said.
* #437 touched THREE src/ files, not one: diskimage.c, diskimage_scsicmd.c, diskimage.h. 'One src/ COMMIT' was true; the round record should name the three files.
* Q3 NO EMERGENCY RE-RUN for 20ce22e and 7e3b120 -- every changed line is gate 2's surface or non-battery tooling, and the binary is bit-identical by construction, so a full battery would re-measure 14 unchanged gates against an unchanged binary: ritual, not evidence. ONE CHEAP CONDITION: selftest_mutation.sh's own header says run it after any change to gate 2, and that rule was triggered. Run gate 3 once at HEAD.
* Q4 VACUITY, NAMED NOT SURVEYED: (1) gate_asan_sweep is a CONSTRUCTION sweep -- 37 machine types construct under ASan and nothing more, so *** #437's NEW CODE HAS NEVER RUN UNDER ASan ***; (2) gate_hygiene's pattern set contains ZERO occurrences of sync/sense/sd0, so the new guest-visible error class is invisible to it; (3) gate_arm passed 16/16 WITH armbdt PRESENT -- not hypothetical, the measured LDM/STM defect was live at this HEAD; (4) selftest_mutation's green means ONE differential of eleven can fail, and its apparatus carries smhang/smnotland unfixed; (5) gate_ab is coarse rather than vacuous -- marker parity 1:1:1 accepted ~0.44% instruction drift. CHECKED CLEAN: gate_upstream's empty-both-sides hole is closed, gate 5 carries mutant-derived NINSTRS floors, and the old prompt-predicate hole in arm_flags_probe.py is CLOSED (its own 7-day-old memory note claiming otherwise is stale).
* Q5 QUEUE RISK THE BATTERY CANNOT SEE, ranked: armbdt (the only MEASURED defect, battery structurally green over it); idesync (the #437 CLASS on the other disk stack, and the ATA rig boots a ramdisk kernel that issues no flush traffic); b120r; the four wdc residuals including a guest-set malloc count behind CHECK_ALLOCATION; the three selfmutant apparatus items; and m437multi carries INVERTED risk -- the battery now PINS the conservative behaviour that item wants changed, so its fix round must expect a SCHEDULED RED, not a regression.

rows.title: idesync  IDE FLUSH CACHE has no durability path at all -- #437 is SCSI-only

entries.note: grep -i flush src/devices/dev_wdc.c returns NOTHING, so a guest's ATA FLUSH CACHE is not merely unflushed but unimplemented. Reachability UNKNOWN; landisk is the ATA rig and it boots, so a probe witness is likely available.  [panel_20260818_095322]

*** THE BRIEF'S FRAMING WAS HALF WRONG, AND THE HALF IT GOT WRONG CHANGES WHAT SHOULD BE FIXED. *** Verdict FIX-not-document, but not for the reason I gave it.
* 0xE7 WDCC_FLUSHCACHE is DEFINED at wdcreg.h:130 and NEVER REFERENCED in dev_wdc.c; 0xEA has no constant anywhere in src/. Both fall to wdc_command()'s default:, which sets WDCE_ABRT, emits an UNLATCHED fatal(), and -- the part that matters -- does NOT set d->int_assert. MEASURED offline against the shipping wdc_command(): 0xE7 -> err=0x04 irq=0 fatal=1, status 0x51 (DRDY|DSC|ERR), against the 0x10 RECAL control at err=0x00 irq=1.
* NO REAL GUEST ISSUES IT, and the negative is WELL CONTROLLED. With an IDE disk attached and a full filesystem lifecycle (MAKEDEV, fdisk, disklabel, newfs 64 MB FFS, mount, write, sync, umount, halt -p) OpenBSD 7.6 issues exactly: 0xEC 0xF5 0x10 0x91 0xC6 0x20 0xC4 0x30 0xC5 0xE0. No 0xE7, no 0xEA.
* IT REFUTED ITS OWN LEADING HYPOTHESIS rather than resting on it: 'the drive does not advertise FLUSH CACHE' was tested with TWO discriminating IDENTIFY variants (word 83=0x5000 and 0x7000). The guest DEMONSTRABLY READ the new IDENTIFY -- it began issuing 0xEF SET FEATURES, which it never did before -- and STILL never flushed. Why OpenBSD declines is an honest UNKNOWN: there is no OpenBSD source in this tree, and reconstructing wd_flushcache from memory is exactly the trap the SH-manual rule exists to prevent.
* *** THE LIVE DEFECT IS THE ARM, NOT THE OPCODE: 0xE0 STANDBY IMMEDIATE hits the same default: on EVERY `halt -p`, measured 4 of 4 shutdown runs. *** ABRT to the guest, no interrupt, unlatched host warning, and the guest swallows it silently. So the IDE side has a reachable reproducible fall-through TODAY, and FLUSH CACHE is an unreached member of the same set.
* THE FIX IS NOT A ONE-LINER. diskimage_sync() takes a struct diskimage *, but dev_wdc.c only ever holds (machine, id, type) -- and THERE IS NO EXPORTED (machine,id,type) -> struct lookup; every public function in diskimage.c open-codes the same 6-line walk. Needs a diskimage_sync_id() wrapper, a WDCC_FLUSHCACHE_EXT constant, and a case arm that also sets int_assert. Built privately: 0xE7/0xEA become err=0x00 irq=1 fatal=0 with trace F(data) S(data), matching the SCSI sibling.
* DETECTOR BUILT, and it COMPILES AGAINST BOTH TREES because the rows pass a RAW OPCODE INTEGER rather than the WDCC_ constant -- deliberately sidestepping the exact trap diff_diskimage_sync.c's header records, where naming the new symbol made the pre-fix arm a SETUP result. 9 rows / 0 failed pre-fix; 8 of 9 flip post-fix. Needs only two extra stubs given the flags gate_offline.sh already passes.
* SCOPE: all three files are byte-identical between est/ and GXEMUL-SEC/. And wdc is far from landisk-only -- bus_isa, bus_pci, dev_pcic, dev_ps2_spd, machine_arc.c:235, machine_landisk.c:87 and promemul/of.c all instantiate it, so ARC IS A SECOND ATA RIG THAT WAS NOT TESTED.  [agent idesync 2026-08-19]

*** DOCUMENT, DO NOT FIX -- AND THE DECIDING FACT IS ONE NOBODY RAISED: THE DRIVE NEVER ADVERTISES FLUSH CACHE. ***  The highest IDENTIFY word wdc_initialize_identify_struct() writes is 68. Words 82-87 -- the COMMAND SET SUPPORTED / ENABLED block -- are left ZERO by the opening memset. A device that advertises no command sets and aborts a command it never claimed is not obviously wrong. On that reading idesync is a MISSING FEATURE, not a durability defect, and the 'correct' fix is a much larger IDENTIFY change that collides with diff_wdc_identify.c's explicit frozen-scope banner (#405/#407/#408/#410/#411).

The negative control is stronger than claimed and still does not rescue the row: word 83 = 0x5000/0x7000 sets the validity marker plus the flush bits, the guest demonstrably read the new block, and it STILL never flushed. With words 82, 85 and 86 zero the block is internally inconsistent, which is a plausible reason a driver would decline -- but that is a HYPOTHESIS, and 'why OpenBSD declines' remains an honest UNKNOWN.

The wrapper claim is CHECKED TRUE: diskimage.c open-codes the machine->first_diskimage walk TWELVE times (:113, 321, 340, 360, 385, 1558, 2120, 2130, 2149, 2177, 2198, 2310); a diskimage_sync_id() would be the thirteenth.

Cost: a new public export, a new constant, two case arms and a detector that can only ever be construction-tested -- against a command NO GUEST IN THIS TREE ISSUES and which the model CORRECTLY DECLINES TO ADVERTISE. Worst ratio of the five rows. witness: none.

rows.title: wdcnoirq  wdc_command()'s default: arm asserts no interrupt, so an interrupt-driven guest waits for a completion that never comes

entries.note: MEASURED. The arm sets WDCE_ABRT and returns without setting d->int_assert, and dev_wdc_tick() raises the IRQ only when that flag is set. A polling driver sees ABRT; an interrupt-driven one sees nothing at all. Live TODAY via 0xE0 on every halt -p, not only via the unimplemented flush. That an interrupt-waiting driver would then hit a wdc timeout is READ/inference -- no guest was observed doing it.  [agent idesync 2026-08-19]

rows.title: smhang  selfmutant.py has NO TIMEOUT: a hanging mutant wedges gate 2 with no verdict token at all

entries.note: MEASURED by the ninth seat: build_and_run()'s subprocess.run carries no timeout, so a mutant that loops forever (`for (;;)` inside sh4_timer_tick) produces NO SELFMUTANT_* token -- not OK, not FAIL, not SETUP -- and the gate wedges. The dead-man switch then reports 'battery NEVER RAN', unattributed. #55's filed taxonomy for gate 3 was crash/timeout/empty; selfmutant.py closed crash (F5) and empty output and left TIMEOUT WITH NO ARM. Fix: timeout= on the run and the build, TimeoutExpired -> SETUP. Group with `smnotland`; both fixes are a dozen lines together.

PANEL RECORDED ON smnotland, not here -- one panel assessed both rows and splitting the record across two rows is the exact error two gates caught last round. *** THE FLAGSHIP SEAT RULED THIS ROW SHOULD BE ITS OWN ROUND, and the ruling was accepted on the reopening rule's objective prong: a detector for this defect must assert 'SETUP within T seconds', which is a WALL-CLOCK ORACLE, and the rule admits a second site only with no new oracle. *** The FIX nevertheless landed together, because it is the same two functions and the measure seat's validated prototype demonstrated one design covers both -- measurement over reasoning on the prong itself. What is deferred is this row's own REGRESSION ROW, which is where the wall-clock oracle would enter. Recorded so the grouping reads as a decision rather than an oversight.

*** RULED THIS SHOULD BE ITS OWN ROUND, and the ruling is accepted. ***  On the reopening rule's objective prong: a detector for this defect must assert 'SETUP within T seconds', which is a WALL-CLOCK ORACLE -- the class this project's records treat as most dangerous -- and the rule admits a second site only with NO NEW ORACLE. It also rejected the ledger's own grouping argument ('both fixes are a dozen lines together') as a SIZE argument, which is not one of the prongs. Separately it found that `timeout=` as I specified it is not enough for the BUILD phase, and that `start_new_session` is what makes killpg safe -- without it the children share the GATE's process group and killpg is gate suicide. Its stated MECHANISM (a blocking post-kill drain) was measured FALSE on POSIX; the conclusion held for a different reason.

DERIVED THE TIMEOUTS FROM MEASUREMENT rather than choosing them: slowest build across all 12 lanes 1.37 s, slowest run 0.31 s, on an idle machine. Recommends build=120 s (~88x) and run=60 s (~190x), SEPARATE, env-overridable -- separate because the diagnoses differ (a two-minute compile means the host is sick; a spinning run is the EXPECTED mutant outcome) and because the SETUP message must name the phase. On margin it cited this project's own gate_ab, which uses 3x and measurably false-FAILed a 45-minute battery under load, so 3x is KNOWN-INSUFFICIENT here. It measured the process-group kill both ways: run(timeout=) returned at 3.00 s and left the spinner alive; Popen(start_new_session)+killpg reaped the whole tree, child pgid 32 against the gate's 11, so killpg provably cannot reach the gate. It also found THREE MORE no-token paths with no hang at all -- a subject path typo, a missing fragment file, a wrong argument count -- each a traceback with no token, and noted that `if not failtok` printed FAIL even when stdout had NO token, a case gate_offline.sh:913-925 records being measured before and which was fixed in two detectors rather than in the helper.

Insisted build and run get SEPARATE, MEASURED, env-overridable budgets for the same reason the measure seat did -- the build is one -O2 TU where DrvFs/WSL variance is real, the run is the semantics under test and the only phase that can spin. It also flagged the cleanup interaction: the try/finally rmtree unlinks a still-running mutant's binary, so the kill must precede the finally or a spinner is orphaned onto the host, which is the load-sensitive wall-clock hazard. Measured after the fix: 0 orphans.

Agreed the hang is real and that expiry must be SETUP rather than FAIL, and treated the no-token state as the same contract violation the helper's own docstring already names ('no verdict token' is listed as a SETUP cause and the code did not deliver it).
'Do not share a budget; bound by the gate, not by slowest plus slack.' Adopted verbatim as the design rule. It reached the separate-budget conclusion independently of the two measuring seats.
